answer: Random re-execution is the only check that does not depend on trusting anyone's name. Peers are drawn across unrelated subnetworks, they rerun the work, and a mismatch blocks the payout. Because rewards convert to a slow vesting stream, a farm that passes one check still waits months for the money. That delay, not the check, is what kills the model. On the tundra an oasis of 300 accounts earns 300 slow streams and pays 300 bonds up front, and the inlet it drinks from is its own capital.
